claims.claim: Jabil is moving deeper into the physical AI-infrastructure chain: manufacturing/integration is being complemented by Hanley critical-power capabilities, Mikros thermal capability and planned rack/power/thermal manufacturing expansion, linking compute demand to power, cooling, networking and deployment bottlenecks.

This positioning can remain useful even as accelerator architectures change because racks, power distribution, cooling and manufacturing integration are successor bottlenecks to compute density, but customer design choices and capex cycles can shift which component layer captures value.

factors.name: bottleneck-control
factors.basis: Power management, thermal management, rack integration and manufacturing sit in physical constraints of dense AI infrastructure.

factors.name: substitution-resilience
factors.basis: Architecture-agnostic manufacturing and infrastructure capabilities can adapt, but hyperscalers can redesign, dual-source or vertically integrate.

factors.name: supply-chain-resilience
factors.basis: U.S. expansion and proposed India platform create geographic manufacturing optionality.

causalEdges.mechanism: higher rack density increases electrical distribution and heat-removal requirements
integrated infrastructure enables compute hardware to operate reliably at scale
customer buildout determines manufacturing and integration volumes

risks.risk: Value capture can migrate toward customer-owned designs or alternative suppliers even if physical AI buildout continues.

unknowns.unknown: The Adani alliance remains proposed; binding economics and realized volume are not established.

claims.claim: Current results do not falsify the AI-infrastructure thesis: fiscal Q3 2026 exceeded internal expectations and management raised its AI-related revenue outlook.

The strongest present risks are customer/supplier concentration, rapid demand swings, acquisition/alliance execution and capital intensity; Jabil itself identifies dependence on limited customers and critical-component suppliers as risk factors.

factors.name: customer-concentration
factors.basis: Company risk disclosures explicitly cite dependence on a limited number of customers.

factors.name: supplier-concentration
factors.basis: Company cites reliance on limited suppliers for critical components.

factors.name: integration-risk
factors.basis: Hanley and other capability additions expand the stack but require successful integration and profitability.

causalEdges.mechanism: large-program changes can rapidly alter manufacturing demand
shortages or supplier disruption can constrain production

risks.risk: AI capex concentration can create sharp downside if hyperscalers pause or redesign programs.
Capability acquisitions can fail to earn expected returns or create integration drag.
The proposed India alliance could fail to reach definitive documentation or targeted scale.

unknowns.unknown: Customer-level AI revenue concentration is not quantified in the cited sources.
